summary: Presence analytics now derives real routes: a ground-truth speed computed from consecutive fixes (never Life360's own mostly-empty speed field), named corridors clustered from the road-name sequences Life360 already sends, and per-corridor speed percentiles by hour-of-week — a congestion model built entirely from a subject's own history.
details: A trip is the movement between two confirmed stays; a corridor is a named cluster of trips whose road-name sequences are close by edit distance.
Corridor identity is a durable id, preserved across re-clustering the same way Tier 3's place identity fix established — a corridor does not churn a new id every cycle.

An address-less trip can never mint or contaminate a corridor: clustering partitions trips into named and address-less groups before either the initial-cluster or the noise-join pass runs, because an empty road-name sequence is a similarity-neighbour of nearly any short real corridor under edit distance.
limitations: A trip's still-ambiguous tail (has not yet resolved into a closed stay or continued movement) is never extracted early — a small sliver at that exact seam is accepted as lost, not guessed.
Corridor and speed-percentile data has no consumer yet, matching Tier 3's own posture — nothing reads presence_trips/presence_corridors/presence_corridor_speed outside this substrate today.

Trip extraction has no analogous protection to a stay's own settled_seconds withholding of an open stay: the analytics tick (nora/analytics/__main__.py's _tick) fires on cadence alone and does not yet implement DEC-115's three fire conditions (safety_lag backlog, settled_seconds quiet boundary, max_age_seconds), a pre-existing gap from Tier 1 that Tier 5 inherits rather than introduces. Under real driving conditions this can fragment one continuous trip into many short spurious trips, and at corridor_max_edit_distance=2 over the resulting short road-name sequences, genuinely distinct routes can collapse into one corridor. Tier 5's derivation logic and storage are built and tested against the trip/corridor data model itself, but this means the corridor/speed-percentile data is not yet reliable at scale until the tick's fire conditions are fixed — a separate, not-yet-made design decision.
